result: All 6 tests pass (exit code 0). There were two bugs in the `inventory` package. The first was in `inventory/pricing.py:10` (`discounted_unit_price`): the category discounts are stored as percents (e.g. 15 means 15% off), but the code computed `unit_price_cents * (1 - pct)`, treating the percent as a fraction of 1 — so any nonzero discount flipped the price negative (seasonal 15 → ×−14, clearance 40 → ×−39), which broke `test_seasonal_discount`, `test_clearance_line_total`, and `test_inventory_value`. I fixed it to `unit_price_cents * (1 - pct / 100)`. The second bug was in `inventory/report.py:8` (`top_lines`): it sorted by `line_total` ascending and took the first `n`, returning the *cheapest* lines instead of the highest, contrary to its docstring. Notably, `test_top_lines` was passing before only by coincidence — the negative prices from the first bug made the ascending sort happen to yield `["C3", "B2"]`, so fixing pricing alone would have broken that test. I fixed it by adding `reverse=True` so the list comes back highest-first; no files under `tests/` or `run_tests.py` were touched.
